# Engine guide (AGENT_GUIDE)

The engine's own authoring reference — the same text its AI panel and

# Engine API — LLM Reference

> 2D vector design engine. Objects sharing the same `name` across scenes auto-morph.

---

## 2. Scenes

A scene holds objects + a background `style` (fills/strokes/effects) + `motion` (navigation transitions §8 + the timeline clock declaration §10) + `clip`. Operate via the `*_scene` ops (create_scene/update_scene/delete_scene/duplicate_scene/move_scene/set_scene_size); `update_scene` `set` keys: name/description/notes/style/visible/motion/data/clip. `clip:true` masks the scene's content to the canvas bounds (stored as `data.clip`). "this scene" / "current scene" = the one with `active:true` in the provided state.
Defaults: name `'New Scene'`, fills white solid, `clip:false` (objects may overflow the canvas visibly).

---

## 3. Objects

An object has `name`, `size`, `transform`, `style`, `opacity`, `visible`, `blendMode`, `motion`, type-specific `data`, and (groups/frames) `children`. Create with `create_object`; change with `update_object` (`set` keys: name/size/transform/style/opacity/blendMode/visible/locked/motion/interaction/distort/layout/data) and the object ops (delete/duplicate/move/group/ungroup/convert_to_path).

Common defaults: `size 100×100`, `transform { x:0,y:0,z:0, rotateX:0,rotateY:0,rotateZ:0, scaleX:1, scaleY:1, skewX:0, skewY:0, anchorX:0.5, anchorY:0.5, perspective:0 }`, fills `#000000` solid, `opacity:1`, `visible:true`, `blendMode:'normal'`.

### Anchor coordinate model

`(x, y)` is where the **anchor point** lands in parent space. `anchorX/Y` are normalized [0..1] in the bounding box.

| anchor | (x, y) means | rotation/scale pivot |
|---|---|---|
| 0,0 | top-left | top-left |
| 0.5,0.5 (default) | center | center |
| 1,1 | bottom-right | bottom-right |

Rules: with default anchor, `x:0,y:0` is NOT top-left — half the object goes off-canvas. `rotateZ` pivots around anchor. Resizing also pivots around anchor (0.5/0.5 grows from center; 0/0 grows right/down). Changing anchor while keeping (x,y) MOVES the object — compensate `(x,y) += size·Δanchor` to preserve on-screen position.

**Relative edits**: read the target's CURRENT value from the provided state, compute the new value, send only the changed field. `set.transform`/`set.size`/`set.data`/`set.layout` MERGE (send only changed keys); `set.style`/`set.distort` REPLACE wholesale. To edit a child of a group, target the child's own id.

### Pin layout (`layout.pin`) — responsive constraints

`layout: { pin: { horizontal: 'left'|'right'|'center'|'stretch'|'scale', vertical: 'top'|'bottom'|'center'|'stretch'|'scale' } }` — defaults left/top. Pins a child's edges to its PIN PARENT — a `frame` (for frame children) or the canvas (for top-level objects) — and re-derives position/size when that parent RESIZES (frame `set.size`, canvas `set_scene_size`). No visual change until a resize happens. A group can BE pinned but cannot be a pin parent.
- `left/top` (default): keep the offset from that edge. `right/bottom`: keep the offset from the opposite edge. `center`: keep the offset from the center. `stretch`: keep BOTH edge offsets (resizes with the parent). `scale`: scale position+size proportionally.
- Recipes: bottom-anchored footer → `vertical:'bottom'`; full-width header bar → `horizontal:'stretch'`; background that follows the canvas → both `'stretch'`.
`{"op":"update_object","id":"<id>","set":{"layout":{"pin":{"horizontal":"stretch","vertical":"bottom"}}}}`

### Distort (4-corner perspective)

`set.distort` REPLACES wholesale: `{ type:'perspective', visible:true, corners:[{x,y},{x,y},{x,y},{x,y}] }` — corners in TL,TR,BR,BL order, each normalized 0..1 of the object's size (identity = {0,0},{1,0},{1,1},{0,1}); `null` clears. Keep corner offsets subtle (±0.05~0.15) for a card-tilt look.
3D tilt: `set.transform.{rotateX,rotateY,z,perspective}` — degrees / px; `perspective` 0 = flat, so give it e.g. 800 with a tilt; a perspective smaller than the object's own depth is silently raised (near-plane clamp) — keep it ≥ 2× the long edge; composes with `distort`; animate via `transform.rotateY` etc. tracks (radians).
`{"op":"update_object","id":"<id>","set":{"distort":{"type":"perspective","visible":true,"corners":[{"x":0.05,"y":0},{"x":0.95,"y":0.08},{"x":1,"y":1},{"x":0,"y":0.92}]}}}`

## 4. Object types

Primitive type strings (the ONLY valid first arg to `createObject`): `'rect' | 'circle' | 'path' | 'text' | 'image' | 'video' | 'audio' | 'group' | 'frame'`. Helper-function names like `lineH`/`lineV`/`text` are NOT primitives.

### 4.1 rect
`size 100×100`, default fill `#000000` solid, `data.radius: [20,20,20,20]` (rounded by default — use `[0,0,0,0]` for sharp). Radius order: [tl, tr, br, bl]. Default anchor 0.5/0.5 → (x,y) is CENTER; for top-left placement set `transform: { anchorX:0, anchorY:0 }`.

### 4.2 circle
`data.innerRadius: 0` (0~1, 0=disk, 0.5=donut). width≠height → ellipse. Same anchor convention as rect.

### 4.3 path
Default fills `[]`, stroke only. Points local to the `size` box.

```js
{ points: [
    { type: 'move', x, y },
    { type: 'line', x, y },
    { type: 'quadratic', cx, cy, x, y },
    { type: 'cubic', cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2, x, y }
  ], closed: true }
```
**Quirk**: leftmost/topmost point MUST be at (0,0). Negative coords cause the engine to shift all points by (-minX,-minY) without compensating `transform.x/y` → visible drift.

### 4.4 image / video / audio
`fills: []`. `image.data.src` HTTPS URL. `video.data`: `src 'asset://id', autoplay, loop, muted, volume, trimIn, trimOut, timelineSync, timelineOffset` (offset = clock ms the synced clip starts at). `audio` placeholder 20×20.

### 4.5 group
Group via `group_objects` (≥2 existing ids); split via `ungroup`. A group's `data.boolean` (`'none'|'mask'|'invertedMask'`) makes the first child clip the rest ('invertedMask' shows OUTSIDE the mask instead). Child (x,y) is local to the group; `move_object` with `options.parentObjectId` (+ `preserveWorldPosition`) re-parents.

### 4.6 frame
A FIXED-SIZE clipping CONTAINER: a styled box (`style.fills`/`strokes`, rounded `data.radius` [tl,tr,br,bl]) that holds `children` and CLIPS them to its bounds when `data.clip` (default true). Defaults: `size 200×200`, white solid fill, `radius [0,0,0,0]`, `clip:true`. Unlike a group its `size` is FIXED (no auto-fit to children). Nest objects by creating the frame FIRST with a self-assigned `config.id`, then each child via `create_object` with `options.parentObjectId` = that id; a child's (x,y) is LOCAL to the frame's top-left (anchor 0/0). Use for cards/containers that must clip overflow. A frame is a PIN PARENT — children with `layout.pin` follow its resizes (see Pin layout).

### 4.7 text — special rules

**Defaults**: `size 100×50`, `fontFamily 'Pretendard'`, `fontSize 26`, `fontWeight 500`, `lineHeight 36`, `textAlign 'left'`, `verticalAlign 'top'`, `autoSize true`, `breakWords true`, `wordWrap true`, default fill `#000000` solid.

```js
data: {
  text, fontSize, fontWeight,           // 100~900 or 'normal'/'bold'
  fontStyle: 'normal'|'italic',
  textDecoration: 'none'|'underline'|'line-through',
  lineHeight, letterSpacing,
  textAlign: 'left'|'center'|'right',
  verticalAlign: 'top'|'middle'|'bottom',
  autoSize: true
}
```

**Two modes — DECIDE FIRST by whether the text must fit inside a fixed box.** Both modes REQUIRE explicit `anchorX/anchorY` in `transform` (F14).
- **autoSize:true** — text sizes to its CONTENT: titles, labels, eyebrows, short single-line copy NOT bounded by a container. Engine measures glyphs, OVERWRITES `size`, and **DISABLES wrapping — a long line just grows wider** (break only with explicit `\n`). Do NOT pass `size`. Anchor MUST match alignment (left→0/center→0.5/right→1, top→0/middle→0.5/bottom→1) or the engine's stale-size compensation drifts (x,y) ~(-50,-25)px; `(x,y)` lands at the alignment-corner.
- **autoSize:false** — text **WRAPS inside a FIXED box**. Use for any BODY / PARAGRAPH that must stay inside a card / panel / column rect. `size.width` is the wrap width — set it to the container's inner width (≈ `cardWidth − 2×padding`); `size.height` must cover the wrapped lines (F4) or it clips (masked to the box). `textAlign`/`verticalAlign` align INSIDE the box; anchor honored as-is (F11). Forbidden: `autoSize:false` WITHOUT `size` (defaults to 100×50, clips); `size.height < lineHeight × lineCount` (clips); `size.width < ~3×fontSize` (one char per line).

**Decision rule (HARD): a multi-sentence body placed inside a card/panel/column MUST be `autoSize:false` with `size.width` = the container's inner width — otherwise it renders as ONE long line and overflows the box into its neighbors. Standalone titles/labels → `autoSize:true`.**

#### Mandatory text formulas (F1–F17, apply in order)

**F1 — typography scale** (set both `fontSize` AND `lineHeight` always; `lineHeight = ceil(fontSize × ratio)`):
| role | fontSize | ratio | letterSpacing |
|---|---|---|---|
| display/hero | 96–200 | 1.10 | -2 to -4 |
| h1 | 56–88 | 1.15 | -1 to -2 |
| h2 | 36–52 | 1.25 | -0.5 to 0 |
| subheading | 24–32 | 1.40 | 0 |
| body | 16–22 | 1.50 | 0 |
| caption | 11–14 | 1.55 | +0.4 to +1.0 |

**F2 — wrap width** (autoSize:false): target `fontSize × 28` (~60 chars). Hard limits `fontSize × 8` ≤ width ≤ `fontSize × 50`.

**F3 — safe area**: `pad = max(48, fontSize × 0.5)`. All visible text inside `[pad, canvasW-pad] × [pad, canvasH-pad]`. Translate by anchor when checking edges.

**F4 — height (autoSize:false)**: `size.height ≥ ceil(lineHeight × maxLines + lineHeight × 0.25)`. Estimate `maxLines = ceil(text.length / floor(size.width / (fontSize × charFactor)))` with `charFactor = 0.55` (Latin) or `1.0` (Korean/CJK).

**F5 — autoSize line breaks**: insert `\n` so each line's estimated width `≤ canvasW - 96` (`width = chars × fontSize × charFactor`). Break at phrase boundaries.

**F6 — hierarchy ratio**: pick base body B (16–22). Sizes: caption `B×0.75`, h3 `B×1.25`, h2 `B×1.7`, h1 `B×2.4`, hero `B×4.5`. No ad-hoc sizes.

**F7 — alignment-anchor consistency in a column**: every text in the same vertical column shares the same `textAlign`.

**F8 — contrast**: dark bg → `#FFFFFF/#F5F5F7/#E5E7EB`. Light bg → `#0F172A/#1F2937`. Never light-grey-on-white or dark-grey-on-black.

**F9 — fontWeight × fontSize**: ≥72 → 700–800 + negative letterSpacing. 16–22 → 400–500. ≤14 → 500–600. Never combine 14/200 or 200/300.

**F10 — Korean/CJK**: only fonts whose `languages` include `ko` (default `Pretendard`). char width factor 1.0. body lineHeight ratio 1.55.

**F11 — anchor MUST be explicit on autoSize:false.** Default anchor 0.5/0.5 means (x,y)=center. Pick ONE pattern:
- Top-left intent: `anchorX:0, anchorY:0` + (x,y)=top-left + textAlign:'left'+verticalAlign:'top'.
- Center intent: default anchor + (x,y)=box center + textAlign:'center'+verticalAlign:'middle'.

**F14 — even autoSize:true MUST get explicit anchor matching alignment.** Engine overrides anchor on first measure and shifts (x,y) by stale-default-size compensation (~(-50,-25) drift). ALWAYS set `anchorX/Y` matching the alignment, regardless of autoSize.

**F15 — coord meaning MUST match alignment**:
- `textAlign:'left'` → x = box LEFT (e.g. `cardX + padding`).
- `textAlign:'center'` → x = box CENTER (e.g. `cardX + cardW/2`).
- `textAlign:'right'` → x = box RIGHT.
- Same for y vs verticalAlign. Mismatching x with textAlign bleeds the box outside the parent by half its width.

**F16 — same-name text across scenes morphs ONLY when content/typography is identical.** Different copy/fontSize/fontWeight under the same name produces "찌그러지면서 모핑" stretch artifact. Suffix per-scene names (`'title-s2'`) when content differs → clean cross-fade. Same applies to drastically different fontSize/weight even with same content. Persistent chrome (logo, page number, sticky header) uses stable name + IDENTICAL spec.

**F16-PERF**: name-reuse pre-boosts target glyph atlas to `peak = parent × max(|fromScale|,|toScale|)`. Big fontSize jumps (e.g. 96→360) allocate multi-MB atlas → mobile jank. Persistent chrome with identical fontSize is fine; everything else gets per-scene suffix.

**F16-MOTION**: don't strip ALL motion by suffixing every name. Use **two name buckets per scene**:
- Bucket A — persistent chrome that morphs (4–8 per scene-pair): background `rect`, accent-bar `rect`, rule lines, page-frame outline, persistent underline, brand mark image. These provide the morph feel.
- Bucket B — scene-specific TEXT (unique `-sN` suffix): titles/body/captions cross-fade cleanly.

**F17 — graceful enter/exit via opacity:0 pre-placement.** Pure cross-fade has no transform. To get zoom-fade-in: pre-define same-name object in scene N with `opacity:0` + scaled-down/offset transform (`scaleX/Y:0.85` or `y:targetY+24`), then settle in scene N+1. Zoom-fade-out: mirror. Object content/size MUST be identical (avoid F16 distortion).

**F13 — bounds & overlap self-check before emitting**: compute actual `left/top/right/bottom` for each anchor and verify (1) inside safe area (≥60 padding), (2) no vertical overlap in a column, (3) text fully inside its container with ≥24px padding, (4) row of cards: `right(i) ≤ left(i+1)`. Anchor → bounds: 0/0 → `(x, y, x+w, y+h)`; 0.5/0.5 → `(x-w/2, y-h/2, x+w/2, y+h/2)`; 1/1 → `(x-w, y-h, x, y)`.

#### fontFamily
Set `data.fontFamily` to a name from the **Registerable CDN font catalog** (or one already registered, listed in the state `fonts`) — the engine auto-loads it from the catalog on first use; unknown names fall back to the system font. Korean text → a font whose `languages` include `ko` (default `Pretendard`). Never invent a font name.

## 5. Coordinate space

Origin (0,0) = top-left of scene; X right, Y down; pixels. `set.transform.rotateX/rotateY/rotateZ` are in **degrees** (the engine stores radians internally; the tool layer converts). Center of 1920×1080 = (960, 540) at default anchor.

---

## 6. Style — fill / stroke / effect

**Color values** — string or number ONLY: `'#ff5733'`, `'#fff'`, `'red'`, `'rgba(...)'`, or `0xff5733`. NEVER pass objects (`{r,g,b}`, `{hex}`, `{value}`) — Pixi rejects with "Unable to convert color" and falls back to gray. Opacity is a separate field (`opacity` for solid fills; `alpha` for gradient stops/dropShadow).

```js
// solid fill
{ type:'solid', color:'#FF5733', opacity:1, visible:true }

// linearGradient — start/end normalized 0~1 in bbox
{ type:'linearGradient', start:{x:0,y:0}, end:{x:1,y:1},
  colors:[{offset:0,color:'#FF0000',alpha:1},{offset:1,color:'#0000FF',alpha:1}],
  opacity:1, visible:true }

// radialGradient
{ type:'radialGradient', innerRadius:0, outerRadius:0.5, center:{x:0.5,y:0.5},
  colors:[...], opacity:1, visible:true }

// angularGradient (conic sweep) — `rotation` in radians sets the start angle
{ type:'angularGradient', center:{x:0.5,y:0.5}, rotation:0,
  colors:[...], opacity:1, visible:true }

// diamondGradient (L1-norm / rhombus iso-lines)
{ type:'diamondGradient', innerRadius:0, outerRadius:0.5, center:{x:0.5,y:0.5}, rotation:0,
  colors:[...], opacity:1, visible:true }

// image fill — `src` MUST be an `asset://id` already registered in the project
// (you cannot mint asset ids from generated code; only reuse existing ones).
{ type:'image', src:'asset://id', repeat:false, scale:1, rotation:0, opacity:1, visible:true }

// stroke
{ type:'solid', color:'#000', align:0.5, width:2, opacity:1, visible:true }   // align: 0..1 (0=outside, 0.5=center, 1=inside)
```

Strokes accept the SAME gradient types as fills (linear/radial/angular/diamond) — drop the gradient object into `strokes[]` and add `align`/`width`. `image`/`dynamic` paints gray-fallback ONLY on text (fills and strokes) and on stroke heads; shape strokes render them normally.

### Effects (all need `visible:true`; ≤2 per object; only when user asked)

| effect | properties (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `blur` | `strength:8` (0–100), `quality:4` (1–10) |
| `backdropBlur` | `strength:8`, `quality:4` |
| `dropShadow` / `innerShadow` | `offsetX/Y:4` (-100~100), `blur:4` (0–50), `spread:0`, `quality:8`, `color:'#000'`, `alpha:0.5` |
| `outerGlow` | `blur:8`, `spread:0`, `intensity:1`, `color:'#fff'`, `alpha:0.7` |
| `glass` | `refraction:0.5` (0–2), `chromaticAberration:0.3` (0–2), `tint:0.97` (0–1), `blur:8` (0–100) — needs something behind; fills `[]` or semi-transparent; tint color auto-derived |
| `noise` | `amount:0.2` (0–1), `scale:1`, `monochrome:true`, `seed:0` |
| `adjustment` | `brightness/contrast/saturation/hue/exposure` (-1..1; hue/exposure for color grade). Grading long-tail (emit ONLY when asked): `colorBalance:{shadows|midtones|highlights:{cyanRed,magentaGreen,yellowBlue}}`, `blackAndWhite:{enabled,tint}` |

**Progressive (gradient) blur** — `blur`/`backdropBlur` fade the blur along an axis: `startX/startY` → `endX/endY` (0..1 of the object), with `startStrength`/`endStrength` (0..1 blur multiplier; `1/1` = uniform). Focus blur (sharp top → blurred bottom): `{type:'blur',strength:16,startX:0.5,startY:0,endX:0.5,endY:1,startStrength:0,endStrength:1}`.

Phrasing → effect: glass/liquid/lens/유리/리퀸드 → `glass`. blur/흐리게 → `blur`. gradient blur/점점 흐리게/초점 → progressive blur. backdrop/배경블러 → `backdropBlur`. shadow/그림자 → `dropShadow`. grade/색보정/흑백 → `adjustment`. grain/노이즈 → `noise`.

## 6.5 Variables & data binding (`{{token}}`)

Text content and any paint color can embed `{{name}}` tokens that resolve live at render time. Use for repeating chrome that must stay in sync (page numbers, project/scene titles, a brand color reused across objects).

Create with `create_variable` (`config: { name, type, value }`; type `'string'|'color'|'number'|'boolean'`); change its value with `update_variable` (`set: { value }`) — every reference updates live. System variables can't be deleted/moved.

Reference a variable by wrapping its **name** in `{{ }}`:
```js
// in text content
data:{ text:'{{projectName}} — {{pageNo}}/{{totalPageNo}}', ... }
// in a paint color (solid fill/stroke or a gradient stop)
style:{ fills:[{ type:'solid', color:'{{brand}}', opacity:1, visible:true }], strokes:[], effects:[] }
```

- Escape literal braces with a backslash: `\{\{notice\}\}` renders `{{notice}}`.
- A `{{name}}` bound to a NON-color variable used as a color collapses to gray (Pixi can't parse it) — only `type:'color'` vars belong in color slots.
- **Built-in system variables (always available, read-only):** `{{projectName}}`, `{{sceneName}}`, `{{pageNo}}` (1-based, visible scenes only), `{{totalPageNo}}`. Ideal for a persistent page-number text reused across scenes (give it a stable `name` so it morphs).

---

## 7. Scene morphing

- Same `name` across scenes → matched, all properties (transform/size/style + path `points` + distort corners) interpolate.
- Name only in A → fades out; only in B → fades in.
- Different names → independent (no morph).

Anti-pattern: unique generated names everywhere → kills morph. Persistent elements need stable shared `name`.

---

## 8. Transition

Without a transition, changes **snap**. Set on scene or per-object.

```js
// easing (cubic-bezier)
{ type:'easing', delay:0, easing:{ duration:700, curve:[0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94] } }
// defaults: duration 300, curve [0.25,0,0.05,1], delay 0

// spring
{ type:'spring', delay:0, spring:{ stiffness:100, damping:10, mass:1 } }
```

### Property keys (engine throws on others)

| Entity | Allowed keys |
|---|---|
| **scene** | **only** `'default'`, `'style'` |
| **object** | `'default'`, `'style'`, `'opacity'`, `'transform'`, `'transform.x|.y|.z|.rotateX|.rotateY|.rotateZ|.scaleX|.scaleY|.skewX|.skewY|.anchorX|.anchorY|.perspective'`, `'size'`, `'size.width|.height'` |

Resolution priority: object property → object default → scene property → scene default → snap.

**distort / path / radius morphs ride the `'style'` tween key** (there is no `'distort'` key). Perspective tilt-in: same `name` in both scenes, scene A flat `corners` (identity), scene B tilted `corners`, and a scene `'style'` (or `'default'`) tween — the perspective animates as the user advances.

### Application — put the tween under `motion.transitions`

Apply a transition via the `motion` key of a `set` (update) or `config` (create) — there is no `setMotion()`/`addTransition()` call in tool mode. Scene-level uses `update_scene`; a per-object override uses `update_object`. Re-sending just replaces (no ALREADY_EXISTS).

Scene default tween:
`{"op":"update_scene","sceneId":"...","set":{"motion":{"transitions":{"default":{"type":"easing","easing":{"duration":700,"curve":[0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94]}}}}}}`

Stagger — one `update_object` per object, stepping `delay` (e.g. 60·index):
`{"op":"update_object","sceneId":"...","id":"<id>","set":{"motion":{"transitions":{"default":{"type":"easing","delay":60,"easing":{"duration":700,"curve":[0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94]}}}}}}`

### Named presets (match the Motion panel — prefer these over ad-hoc numbers)

- **Basic** — Linear `[0,0,1,1]` · Ease `[0.25,0.1,0.25,1]` · Ease In `[0.42,0,1,1]` · Ease Out `[0,0,0.58,1]` · Ease In Out `[0.42,0,0.58,1]` (300ms).
- **Smooth** — Soft 500 `[0.4,0,0.2,1]` · Glide 700 `[0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94]` · Cinematic 1000 `[0.65,0,0.35,1]` · Reveal 600 `[0.16,1,0.3,1]` · Exit 400 `[0.7,0,0.84,0]` · Weighty spring 120/26/2.5.
- **Expressive** — Anticipate `[0.68,-0.55,0.27,1.55]` · Overshoot `[0.34,1.56,0.64,1]` · Pull Back `[0.36,0,0.66,-0.56]` (500ms; eased value leaves 0–1 on purpose).
- **Snappy** — Quick 200 `[0.4,0,0.2,1]` · Tap spring 300/22/1 · Pop spring 400/18/1.
- **Bouncy** — Soft Bounce spring 180/12/1 · Playful spring 220/8/1 · Jelly spring 260/6/1.2.
- linear = `[0,0,1,1]`; instant = omit the transition (or set `default` to `null`).

### Principle → preset (all engine-expressible)

- **Slow In / Slow Out** — never `Linear` except mechanical/looping; real motion eases.
- **Role** — an entrance/reveal should **decelerate** (Reveal/Soft/Ease Out); an exit/dismiss should **accelerate** (Exit/Ease In); a same-`name` morph reads ease-in-out (Glide/Ease In Out).
- **Timing = weight** — light/UI 150–250ms (Snappy); calm/premium 500–1000ms (Smooth); heavy = Weighty.
- **Anticipation** — `Anticipate` dips below 0 for a real recoil before the move; hero/emphasis, sparingly.
- **Exaggeration / Overshoot** — `Overshoot` or an underdamped spring (Playful/Jelly) for joy; **no overshoot** for trust/finance.
- **Follow-through / overlapping** — stagger entrances with per-object `delay` (≈ index × 60–120ms) so elements overlap and follow-through, within §12.
- **Mood** — elegant→Glide/Cinematic · playful→Overshoot/Playful · urgent→Quick/Pop · gentle→Soft · heavy→Weighty.

Engine limits (don't attempt): position travels a **straight line** A→B and scale is end-to-end — no curved-arc path, no mid-motion **squash & stretch**; convey weight via easing/spring + stagger. Springs ignore `duration`.

---

## 9. Motion = morph between two scenes

Mental model: animate BETWEEN scenes by adding/duplicating a "next" scene with the end state, sharing object `name` for morph, and putting a transition on the scene(s). The morph plays when the user navigates between scenes — that is not an action you emit; your job is to set the scenes + transitions up correctly. For choreography INSIDE one scene (staged beats on a clock), use the timeline instead (§10) — don't build both for the same movement.

**Every scene needs its own content.** A created or duplicated scene starts EMPTY unless you fill it. If you `duplicate_scene` to carry elements forward, build the SOURCE scene's content FIRST (duplicate copies the current state), then adjust the copy — emit the create_object actions BEFORE the duplicate, never after. For a multi-slide deck, give EACH scene its own create_object actions; never leave a slide empty.

### Four foundational recipes

| Recipe | Pattern |
|---|---|
| Fade-in | Object name only in scene B (engine auto-fades) |
| Slide-in | Same name in both. A: off-canvas + opacity:0. B: final position. (left: `x:-w`; right: `canvasW+w`; top: `y:-h`; bottom: `canvasH+h`) |
| Pop / scale-in | Same name. A: `scaleX/Y:0`, opacity:0. B: 1, opacity:1. Use spring. |
| Color/size/shape morph | Same name, only differing property changes |

### Motion anti-patterns

- Add transition without a "before" scene → nothing visibly changes.
- Unique names per scene → kills morph.
- `>1500ms` durations with springs → springs ignore duration; wait feels broken.
- Stagger total > scene duration → last items animate after next slide starts.
- Animating text `size.width/height` without explicit `'size.width'/'size.height'` keys → won't tween.
- A scene's `motion.transitions` using any key other than `'default'`/`'style'` (e.g. `opacity`/`transform`) → CRASH; those keys are object-only.

---

## 10. Timeline animation (per-scene clock)

The scene's `motion.animations.default` DECLARES a clock; each member object's `motion.animations.default.keyframes` binds property tracks to it. Play mode runs the clock on scene entry; `stops` are PPT-style clicker stop points (playback pauses at each).

```js
// scene — clock declaration (update_scene set.motion)
{ animations: { default: {
    duration: 4000,                                   // ms (default 5000)
    fps: 12,                                          // OPTIONAL frame-grid sampling (stop-motion feel); omit = smooth
    stops: [{ id:'s1', time:1500, label:'beat 2' }],  // self-assign ids ('s1','s2',…)
    workArea: { start:1000, end:2500 },               // OPTIONAL play span ms (AE work area) — play mode runs ONLY this slice; the editor previews the whole clock
    keyframes: { style: [ /* background style keys */ ] }
} } }

// object — tracks riding that clock (update_object set.motion)
{ animations: { default: { keyframes: {
    'transform.x': [{ time:0, value:120 }, { time:1200, value:640, tween:{ type:'easing', easing:{ curve:[0.16,1,0.3,1] } } }],
    'opacity':     [{ time:0, value:0 }, { time:600, value:1 }]
} } } }
```

- Track keys (object): `transform.x` `transform.y` `transform.z` `transform.rotateX` `transform.rotateY` `transform.rotateZ` `transform.scaleX` `transform.scaleY` `transform.skewX` `transform.skewY` `transform.anchorX` `transform.anchorY` `transform.perspective` · `size.width` `size.height` · `opacity` · `style` (whole-style keys) · `style.fills.N`/`style.strokes.N`/`style.effects.N` (ONE paint/effect item per key) · `data.text` (string, discrete step) · `data.points` (path geometry — see below) · `distort` (perspective quad: `{type:'perspective',visible:true,corners:[{x,y}×4]}` TL,TR,BR,BL normalized 0..1, or `null` = flat) · `data.radius.tl` `data.radius.tr` `data.radius.br` `data.radius.bl` · `data.innerRadius` · `data.volume` (video/audio, 0..1). Scene: `style` only. Any other key throws.
- `data.points` (path objects only) keys the WHOLE point array — the shape at that instant, in the path's own local coordinates (NOT re-based to the origin like the document array). Keys whose arrays share a topology (same length, same `type` per index) interpolate vertex-for-vertex WITH their bezier handles, so curves stay curves; add or remove a point between keys and the pair holds the earlier shape instead (no guessed correspondence). Author both keys from the same starting shape and move vertices to morph.
- Values are ENGINE units: x/y/z/size in px, `transform.rotateX/rotateY/rotateZ` in RADIANS (deg × π/180 — the degree bridge applies to `set.transform.rotate*` only, NOT tracks), opacity 0..1, scale 1 = 100%.
- A keyframe's `tween` shapes the segment TOWARD THE NEXT key: `{type:'easing',easing:{curve:[…]}}` (no duration/delay — segment length = key spacing), `{type:'spring',spring:{…}}`, or `{type:'step'}` (hold, then jump — appear/disappear). Omit = default ease. Before the first key / after the last, the track HOLDS that value.
- Recipes: hidden until 1s then fade in → `opacity [{time:1000,value:0},{time:1600,value:1}]`. Slide-in beat → key `transform.x` from off-canvas to rest. Appear at a stop → `step` tween landing on the stop time. Stagger entrances by offsetting key times (index × 100–150ms).
- **Merge rule**: `set.motion` merges per sub-container — a sent `animations` map REPLACES the whole animations map (same for `transitions`); the omitted one is preserved. For ANY animation edit, read the entity's current `motion.animations` from state, modify, and resend the COMPLETE map (`{}` clears it).
- Restraint: ≤6 objects with tracks per scene, 2–3 keys per track, one curve family per scene; respect the §12 feel budgets.

---

## 11. Visual design defaults (apply unless overridden)

- **Palette (60-30-10)**: ≤5 colors per design — 1 background (60%), 1 surface (30%), 1 accent (10%) + text + subtle border. Avoid pure `#000`/`#FFF` for backgrounds (`#0A0A0A`/`#FAFAFA` reads finer).
- **Spacing**: 8px grid (or 4 for fine-tuning). Common insets 48/64/80/96/120.
- **Hierarchy**: ONE hero per slide (largest fontSize, brightest color, or only object with motion).
- **Whitespace**: ≥30% empty.
- **Effect restraint**: ≤1 per object, only when asked.
- **Motion restraint**: 1–3 reveals per slide, one curve per deck.

---

## 12. Motion perf budget (HARD — perf-critical)

- `scene.default.easing.duration` ≤ **1500ms** (cinematic/epic only for 1-of moments).
- Per-object: `(delay + duration)` ≤ **1500ms**.
- `max(obj.delay)` across all objects ≤ **800ms** (compress wave beats: 0/400/800).
- Objects with non-trivial per-object transitions ≤ **6 per scene** (let chrome inherit scene default).

Violations cause "still animating" jank when the user advances mid-transition.
